components.note: 力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.pinyin: Tā de lìqi hěn dà.
example.english: He is very strong.
example.fact: 力 is the root of many words about ability or force: 力气 (physical strength), 努力 (effort), 能力 (ability), 压力 (pressure), 电力 (electric power). As a radical it appears in 动 and 办.

examples.hanzi: 他工作很努力，我们都佩服他的毅力。
examples.pinyin: Tā gōngzuò hěn nǔlì, wǒmen dōu pèifú tā de yìlì.
examples.english: He works hard, and we all admire his willpower.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tǐlì bùrú yǐqián le.
examples.english: My stamina isn't what it used to be.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings: 想, 思, 感; 愚 is a dull mind.
禺 (yú) sounds exactly like 愚; also in 遇 yù, 寓 yù.
虫 (insect) — insects and small creatures: 蚊, 蛇, 蜜; 蠢 is wriggling insects, then stupid.
春 (chūn) is a near sound match for chǔn.

example.hanzi: 那是一个非常愚蠢的决定。
example.pinyin: Nà shì yí gè fēicháng yúchǔn de juédìng.
example.english: That was a very stupid decision.
example.fact: 愚 and 蠢 are both independently “foolish, dull” and get reinforced together in 愚蠢, but 蠢's own etymology — built on 虫 (“insect”), evoking the wriggling, aimless movement of bugs — supplies a vivid, almost literal image behind calling a decision or person “stupid.”

examples.pinyin: Shuō zhèyàng de huà zhēn yúchǔn.
examples.english: It's really foolish to say such things.

examples.pinyin: Tā hòuhuǐ zuòle yúchǔn de shì.
examples.english: He regrets doing something foolish.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire and heat: 灯, 烧, 爆; 炸 is to explode or to fry.
乍 (zhà) sounds exactly like 炸; also in 诈 zhà, 作 zuò, 昨 zuó.
弓 (bow) — bows and tension: 张 stretch, 引 draw, 弯 bend; 弹 is to shoot or spring, and a bullet.
单 (dān) is a loose clue for dàn/tán; compare 禅 chán and 蝉 chán.

example.hanzi: 士兵们在路边发现了一个炸弹。
example.pinyin: Shìbīngmen zài lùbiān fāxiàn le yí gè zhàdàn.
example.english: The soldiers found a bomb by the roadside.
example.fact: 弹 (dàn) alone names any small, self-contained projectile — from 子弹 (“bullet”) to 导弹 (“guided missile”) to 炸弹 here — while 炸 (also seen in 爆炸, also in this batch, rank 714) supplies the “explosive” half, so 炸弹 literally reads as “exploding projectile.”

examples.hanzi: 电影里的炸弹在最后一秒被拆除了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de zhàdàn zài zuìhòu yì miǎo bèi chāichú le.
examples.english: The bomb in the movie was defused at the last second.

examples.hanzi: 机场因为炸弹的警报关闭了。
examples.pinyin: Jīchǎng yīnwèi zhàdàn de jǐngbào guānbì le.
examples.english: The airport was closed because of a bomb alert.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — marks cloth and flags, as in 布 cloth, 帽 hat; 帅 once meant a commander under a flag, now also handsome.

example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn shuài.
example.english: He is very handsome.
example.fact: 帅 is the everyday word for "handsome" for men, while 帅哥 ("handsome guy") can be used to address any young man, like "sir". Its older meaning is commander: 元帅 (marshal), and the red general piece in Chinese chess is 帅.

examples.pinyin: Tā chuān zhè jiàn yīfu zhēn shuài!
examples.english: He looks really handsome in this outfit!

examples.pinyin: Nàge nán yǎnyuán yòu gāo yòu shuài.
examples.english: That actor is both tall and handsome.

components.note: 足 (foot) — marks feet and walking, as in 跑 run, 跳 jump, 路 road; 踢 is kicking.
易 (yì) — loose sound hint (tī vs yì); same part sounds out 锡 xī and 赐 cì.

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
example.english: He likes playing football.
example.fact: 踢 is the verb for football: 踢足球, while basketball uses 打 (打篮球). It is also used for 踢毽子 (shuttlecock kicking) and in 踢被子, kicking off the bedcovers while asleep.

examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn tīdào le zhuōzi.
examples.english: He accidentally kicked the table.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu bǎ qiú tīzǒu le.
examples.english: The puppy kicked the ball away.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and joining, as in 听, 聪, 闻: 联 first meant ears joined, so to link. The part 关 stands in for the traditional shape.
阝 (city, right-side form of 邑) — towns and places: 都, 部, 那, 邮; 邦 is a state or country.
丰 (fēng) is a loose clue; 邦 itself gives bāng to 帮 bāng and 绑 bǎng.

example.hanzi: 美国是一个联邦制国家。
example.pinyin: Měiguó shì yí gè liánbāngzhì guójiā.
example.english: The United States is a federal country.
example.fact: 邦 is an older, literary word for “state, nation” on its own that survives today mainly inside compounds like 联邦 (“federation,” literally “linked/joined states”) and 邦交 (“diplomatic relations between states”), rather than as an everyday standalone word.

examples.hanzi: 联邦政府宣布了新的计划。
examples.pinyin: Liánbāng zhèngfǔ xuānbùle xīn de jìhuà.
examples.english: The federal government announced a new plan.

examples.hanzi: 德国也是一个联邦国家。
examples.pinyin: Déguó yě shì yí ge liánbāng guójiā.
examples.english: Germany is also a federal country.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talk: 说, 论, 请; 评 is to comment and judge.
平 (píng) sounds exactly like 评; also in 苹 píng.
禾 (grain) — the top part, as in 和 and 秋. Memory aid: a woman (女) bending under a bundle of grain; grain plus woman gives 'bend / entrust', now 'appoint'.
女 (woman) — the bottom part and radical, as in 她 she and 妈 mom. Here it hints at a yielding, bending figure rather than a woman.

example.hanzi: 三位评委都给了她很高的分数。
example.pinyin: Sān wèi píngwěi dōu gěi le tā hěn gāo de fēnshù.
example.english: All three judges gave her a very high score.
example.fact: 评委 fuses 评 (“to judge, evaluate,” as in 评论 “commentary”) with 委, short for 委员 (“committee member”) — and despite naming a role tied to a group, 评委 in everyday speech is used just as often for one individual panel judge (一位评委, “one judge”) as for the panel collectively.

examples.pinyin: Píngwěimen zhèngzài tīng tā chànggē.
examples.english: The judges are listening to him sing.

examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi píngwěi shuōhuà hěn kèqi.
examples.english: This judge speaks very politely.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; a guest is a person under your roof.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 路 lù, 洛 luò, 落 luò.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.hanzi: 你太客气了,不用送礼物。
example.pinyin: Nǐ tài kèqi le, bú yòng sòng lǐwù.
example.english: You're too polite, no need to bring a gift.
example.fact: 客气 is the polite half of a fixed conversational pair: the standard reply to 谢谢 ("thank you") is 不客气 ("you're welcome", literally "don't be so polite"), and a host telling a guest 别客气 is inviting them to stop being so formal and just relax.

examples.hanzi: 不用客气，这是我应该做的。
examples.pinyin: Búyòng kèqi, zhè shì wǒ yīnggāi zuò de.
examples.english: You're welcome, it's what I should do.

examples.pinyin: Tā duì kèren zǒngshì hěn kèqi.
examples.english: He is always polite to guests.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 造 is to go and make something.
告 (gào) is a loose sound clue (-ao); also in 浩 hào, 靠 kào.
成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.

example.hanzi: 这场事故造成了严重的交通堵塞。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng shìgù zàochéngle yánzhòng de jiāotōng dǔsè.
example.english: This accident caused severe traffic congestion.
example.fact: 造成 almost always attaches to a negative or neutral consequence — 损失 (loss), 影响 (impact), 堵塞 (congestion) — for a good outcome Chinese reaches instead for 带来 ("to bring") or 产生 ("to produce"), so hearing 造成 primes a listener to expect that something has gone wrong.

examples.pinyin: Dàyǔ zàochéngle hěn duō máfan.
examples.english: The heavy rain caused a lot of trouble.

examples.hanzi: 这个错误可能会造成很大的损失。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge cuòwù kěnéng huì zàochéng hěn dà de sǔnshī.
examples.english: This mistake may cause a big loss.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 经过三年的努力,他终于成功了。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò sān nián de nǔlì, tā zhōngyú chénggōng le.
example.english: After three years of effort, he finally succeeded.
example.fact: 经过 bridges a literal and a figurative sense with the same verb: passing by a physical place (经过一家商店, "pass by a shop") and passing through a stretch of time or effort (经过三年的努力, "after three years of effort") — one word for both a spatial and a temporal journey.

examples.hanzi: 我每天都经过这家面包店。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān dōu jīngguò zhè jiā miànbāodiàn.
examples.english: I pass this bakery every day.

examples.pinyin: Shìqing de jīngguò shì zhèyàng de.
examples.english: This is how the whole thing went.

components.note: 周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.
木 (tree) — a stroke added at the top of a tree marks its tip: the end. Compare 未 wèi with the longer lower stroke.

example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù páshān ba.
example.english: Let's go hiking this weekend.
example.fact: 末 pictures the very tip of a tree — 木 (tree) with a stroke marking its topmost point — so 周末 literally names "the tip of the week." The same 末 marks the tail end of other periods too, as in 月末 ("end of the month") and 年末 ("year-end").

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò nǐ yǒu shénme dǎsuan?
examples.english: What are your plans for the weekend?

examples.hanzi: 我们周末常常去看望爷爷奶奶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò chángcháng qù kànwàng yéye nǎinai.
examples.english: We often visit grandpa and grandma at weekends.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
口 (mouth) — speaking, shouting: 叫, 吗, 喊; 号 is to call out, then a call-sign or number.
丂 (kǎo) is only a loose clue; it also appears in 考 kǎo and 巧 qiǎo.

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ méiyǒu shǒujī xìnhào.
example.english: There's no cell phone signal here.
example.fact: 信号 spans both the literal (a WiFi or cell signal, a traffic light) and the figurative (释放信号, "to send a signal/hint") — much like English "signal" moves easily between electronics and body language without needing separate words.

examples.pinyin: Hónglǜdēng de xìnhào biàn le.
examples.english: The traffic light signal has changed.

examples.pinyin: Shān lǐ de shǒujī xìnhào hěn chà.
examples.english: The cell phone signal in the mountains is poor.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.

example.pinyin: Jīnwǎn tiānshang yǒu hěn duō xīngxing.
example.english: There are lots of stars in the sky tonight.
example.fact: 星 appears in 星期 (week) and its days (星期一…), in 明星 (celebrity, "bright star"), and in hotel ratings: 五星级. The stars themselves are counted with 颗: 一颗星.

examples.hanzi: 你知道哪一个明星最有名吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào nǎ yí gè míngxīng zuì yǒumíng ma?
examples.english: Do you know which star is the most famous?

examples.pinyin: Huǒxīng lí dìqiú hěn yuǎn.
examples.english: Mars is very far from Earth.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and walking: 跑, 路, 跳; 跟 first meant the heel, then to follow.
艮 (gèn) is a near sound match for gēn; same part in 根 gēn, 很 hěn, 恨 hèn.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and walking: 跑, 跳, 路; 踪 is a footprint or trace.
宗 (zōng) sounds exactly like 踪; also in 综 zōng and 棕 zōng.

example.hanzi: 警察在跟踪那个嫌疑人。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài gēnzōng nàge xiányírén.
example.english: The police are tailing that suspect.
example.fact: Both halves of 跟踪 are built on 足 ("foot"): 跟 originally named the heel — later "to follow on someone's heels" — and 踪 named the footprints left behind, so the compound literally strings together "heel" and "footprint" as two foot-based images for the same act of tracking someone.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén yìzhí zài gēnzōng wǒ.
examples.english: Someone has been following me.

examples.hanzi: 这个软件可以跟踪你的快递。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ gēnzōng nǐ de kuàidì.
examples.english: This app can track your parcel.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — drinking and speaking: 吃, 吸, 呼; 喝 is to drink.
曷 (hé) sounds exactly like 喝; also in 渴 kě thirsty and 歇 xiē.
酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks and flavors: 醉 drunk, 醒 sober, 酸 sour, 配 match; 酒 is liquor, with 氵 for the liquid.
酉 also hints at the sound: yǒu is close to jiǔ.

example.hanzi: 他晚上喜欢跟朋友喝酒。
example.pinyin: Tā wǎnshang xǐhuan gēn péngyou hējiǔ.
example.english: He likes drinking with friends in the evening.
example.fact: 喝酒 is the default, unmarked way to say "to drink" in a social context — bare 喝 usually needs an explicit object to be clear (喝水, 喝茶) — so asking a friend "喝了没" ("have you had a drink") is often understood by convention to mean alcohol specifically, even without saying 酒.

examples.pinyin: Bàba bù hējiǔ, zhǐ hē chá.
examples.english: Dad doesn't drink alcohol, only tea.

examples.pinyin: Kāichē yǐhòu bù néng hējiǔ.
examples.english: You can't drink alcohol if you're driving.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 推 is to push.
隹 (zhuī) is a loose hint for tuī; 堆 duī and 谁 shéi share it.

example.pinyin: Qǐng tuī yíxià mén.
example.english: Please push the door.
example.fact: 推 is the opposite of 拉 (lā), the pair printed on shop doors. It also means to recommend (推荐), postpone (推迟), refuse (推辞) and deduce (推理).

examples.pinyin: Tā yònglì tuīkāi le mén.
examples.english: He pushed the door open with force.

examples.hanzi: 朋友给我推荐了一家好餐厅。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou gěi wǒ tuījiàn le yì jiā hǎo cāntīng.
examples.english: A friend recommended a good restaurant to me.

components.note: 关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals and tools: 钱, 钢, 铁; 键 is a metal bar or key.
建 (jiàn) sounds exactly like 键; also in 健 jiàn.

example.hanzi: 解决问题的关键是找到原因。
example.pinyin: Jiějué wèntí de guānjiàn shì zhǎodào yuányīn.
example.english: The key to solving the problem is finding the cause.
example.fact: 键 originally named a metal bolt or pin that locks a mechanism shut (built on 钅, "metal") — so 关键 literally combines "the bolt (键) that closes a gate (关)", the single pin without which a whole mechanism fails, behind today's abstract sense of "the crucial point."

examples.pinyin: Guānjiàn shì nǐ yào yǒu xìnxīn.
examples.english: The key is that you need to be confident.

examples.hanzi: 这是比赛中最关键的一分。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì bǐsài zhōng zuì guānjiàn de yì fēn.
examples.english: This is the most crucial point in the match.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
欠 (open mouth, lack) — yawning, breathing and wanting: 歌 song, 欢 joy, 吹 blow; 次 also sounds out 资 zī and 瓷 cí.

example.pinyin: Xiàcì wǒmen zǎodiǎn chūfā.
example.english: Next time let's leave a bit earlier.
example.fact: 次 is Mandarin's measure word for a countable occurrence (一次, 两次, "once, twice"). 下次 substitutes 下 ("next, following") for a number before that same counter, the same pattern behind 上次 ("last time") and 这次 ("this time").

examples.pinyin: Xià cì wǒ qǐng nǐ chīfàn.
examples.english: Next time I'll treat you to a meal.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xià cì shénme shíhou lái?
examples.english: When will you come next time?

components.note: 亠 (lid) — the top part, a cap. Memory aid: a lid on top of 允 suggests something filled up to the lid, hence 'fill, be full' as in 充满.
允 (yǔn, permit) — the bottom part; it is a visible piece, but not a sound clue today (充 is chōng). Memory aid: allowed to fill up.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 满 is filled with water, full.
The right half is a short form of 㒼 (mǎn), the sound part, also in 瞒 mán.

example.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ chōngmǎnle xiàoshēng.
example.english: The room was filled with laughter.
example.fact: 充满 almost always takes an abstract or sensory noun as its object — sound, emotion, hope (充满希望) — rather than a countable physical object; "the box is full of apples" reaches instead for 装满, built on 装 ("to pack, load").

examples.pinyin: Tā de xīnlǐ chōngmǎnle xīwàng.
examples.english: His heart was full of hope.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì chōngmǎnle huólì.
examples.english: This city is full of energy.

components.note: 斤 (axe) — 斤 is an axe, as in 新, 析; 断 is to cut through, shown by the axe and threads cut.

example.pinyin: Shǒujī xìnhào tūrán duàn le.
example.english: The phone signal suddenly cut out.
example.fact: 断 is for things that break in two or are cut off, such as ropes, lines and connections: 断电 (power cut), 绳子断了 (the rope snapped), 不断 (continuously, "not breaking"), 判断 (to judge).

examples.pinyin: Shùzhī bèi dàfēng chuīduàn le.
examples.english: The branch was snapped by the strong wind.

examples.hanzi: 电话突然断了，我没听清楚。
examples.pinyin: Diànhuà tūrán duàn le, wǒ méi tīngqīngchu.
examples.english: The call suddenly cut off, and I couldn't hear clearly.

components.note: 其 (its) — an old picture of a winnowing basket (箕 jī adds bamboo). Sound clue: 期 qī, 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī, 基 jī.
它 (it) — an old picture of a snake; 蛇 shé (snake) adds 虫. Its pronoun use is borrowed. Sound series: 拖 tuō, 驼 tuó.

example.hanzi: 除了这个,还有其它办法吗?
example.pinyin: Chúle zhège, hái yǒu qítā bànfǎ ma?
example.english: Besides this, are there other ways?
example.fact: 其它 is essentially interchangeable with the far more common 其他 — the only difference is the final character's radical, 它 (originally a snake, generalized to "it" for non-human things) versus 他 (the person radical). Some style guides reserve 其它 for non-human "others" and 其他 for everything, though most writers don't bother with the distinction.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu qítā wèntí le.
examples.english: I have no other questions.

examples.hanzi: 桌子上还有其它东西吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng hái yǒu qítā dōngxi ma?
examples.english: Is there anything else on the table?

meanings: to put off a discussion until later

components.note: 冉 (rǎn) — the main part. The dictionary story is two fish on a line 一: a second catch, so 'again'. It is a memory aid; the origin is unclear.
一 (one) — the top bar. Memory aid: 'one more' line on top — 再见 see you again, 再次 once more.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒmen yǐhòu zàishuō.
example.english: Let's talk about this matter later.
example.fact: 再说 does double duty as a literal verb phrase — deferring something to later (以后再说, "we'll talk about it later") — and as a connective at the start of a new clause meaning "moreover, besides" (再说,他也不同意, "besides, he doesn't agree either"). The same two characters cover both a concrete postponement and an abstract argumentative pivot.

examples.hanzi: 今天太忙了，再说我也不想去。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tài máng le, zàishuō wǒ yě bù xiǎng qù.
examples.english: I'm too busy today, and besides I don't want to go.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服太贵了，再说颜色也不适合我。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài guì le, zàishuō yánsè yě bú shìhé wǒ.
examples.english: This piece of clothing is too expensive, and besides the color doesn't suit me.

components.note: 穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.

example.pinyin: Píngzi shì kōng de.
example.english: The bottle is empty.
example.fact: 空 has two readings: kōng (empty, sky: 空气, 天空, 空调) and kòng (free time or empty space: 有空, 空位). "你有空吗?" (Are you free?) therefore uses kòng.

examples.hanzi: 你有空吗？我们去喝咖啡吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu kòng ma? Wǒmen qù hē kāfēi ba.
examples.english: Are you free? Let's go for coffee.

examples.hanzi: 天空很蓝，一朵云也没有。
examples.pinyin: Tiānkōng hěn lán, yì duǒ yún yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: The sky is blue, without a single cloud.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打 hit, 拿 take, 把 hold; 抱 is to hug or hold in the arms.
包 (bāo) is a close sound clue for bào; it also sounds out 跑 pǎo, 饱 bǎo and 炮 pào.

example.pinyin: Māma bàozhe háizi.
example.english: Mom is holding the child.
example.fact: 抱 is to hold something in the arms, and 拥抱 is a hug. It extends to emotions: 抱歉 (sorry, "hold regret"), 抱怨 (complain) and 抱希望 (hold hope).

examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ xiǎomāo bào zài huái lǐ.
examples.english: He held the kitten in his arms.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bào nǐ yíxià.
examples.english: I want to give you a hug.

meanings: to go to the bottom of a matter
when all is said and done

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — holes and hollows: 空, 窗, 突; digging into a cave is investigating to the bottom.
九 (jiǔ) sounds exactly like 究 jiū.
音 (sound) — a piece of music 音 played to its end by a person 儿: finishing, then "at last" or unexpectedly.

example.pinyin: Nǐ jiūjìng xiǎng shuō shénme?
example.english: What exactly are you trying to say?
example.fact: 究竟 intensifies a question, pushing past evasion or confusion toward the real, final answer (你究竟想说什么, "what are you REALLY trying to say") — that insistent, get-to-the-bottom-of-it flavor sets it apart from its closest synonym 到底, though the two are often interchangeable in casual speech.

examples.pinyin: Tā jiūjìng qù nǎr le?
examples.english: Where on earth did he go?

examples.pinyin: Jiūjìng shì shéi dǎpòle bēizi?
examples.english: Who exactly broke the cup?

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 祝你有一个美好的未来。
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ yǒu yígè měihǎo de wèilái.
example.english: I wish you a beautiful future.
example.fact: 美好 is reserved almost exclusively for abstract, positive things — a future, a memory, a wish, a life (美好的回忆, 美好的生活) — and essentially never describes a person's or object's physical appearance, where 漂亮 or 好看 take over instead; mixing the two up is a common learner slip.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng hěn měihǎo.
examples.english: The scenery here is lovely.

examples.hanzi: 我们有一段美好的回忆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu yí duàn měihǎo de huíyì.
examples.english: We share a beautiful memory.

components.note: 王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — a blade 刂 cutting two jades apart: to divide into groups, hence class or shift.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen bān yǒu èrshí gè xuésheng.
example.english: There are twenty students in our class.
example.fact: 班 is a class or group (我们班, 班长), and also a work shift: 上班 (go to work), 下班 (get off work), 加班 (work overtime). It counts scheduled services too: 航班 (flight), 班车 (shuttle bus).

examples.hanzi: 我明天要上班，不能休息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào shàngbān, bùnéng xiūxi.
examples.english: I have to go to work tomorrow and can't rest.

examples.hanzi: 他每天坐第一班地铁上班。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān zuò dì-yī bān dìtiě shàngbān.
examples.english: He takes the first subway every day to work.

meanings: measure word for planes and pianos

components.note: 木 (wood) — wooden things: 桌, 板, 桥; 架 is a wooden frame or rack.
加 (jiā) is a near sound match for jià; also in 驾 jià and 嘉 jiā.

example.pinyin: Shūjià shang yǒu hěn duō shū.
example.english: There are many books on the bookshelf.
example.fact: 架 is a frame or rack (书架 bookshelf) and a measure word for machines and instruments such as planes and pianos: 一架飞机, 一架钢琴. 吵架 and 打架 (quarrel, fight) use it too, and 摆架子 means to put on airs.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen mǎi le yí jià xīn gāngqín.
examples.english: We bought a new piano.

examples.pinyin: Tiānshang fēiguò yí jià fēijī.
examples.english: A plane flew across the sky.

components.note: 圣 (holy) — traditional 聖 had an ear 耳 and a mouth 口: the sage who listens and speaks wisely.

example.pinyin: Shèngdàn Jié kuàilè!
example.english: Merry Christmas!
example.fact: 圣 means holy or sage: 圣人 (sage), 神圣 (sacred), 圣经 (the Bible). 圣诞节 is Christmas, literally "holy birth festival", and 圣诞老人 is Santa Claus.

examples.hanzi: 圣诞节那天，我们一起吃大餐。
examples.pinyin: Shèngdànjié nàtiān, wǒmen yìqǐ chī dàcān.
examples.english: On Christmas Day, we eat a big meal together.

examples.hanzi: 他们去教堂参观那座圣殿。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen qù jiàotáng cānguān nà zuò shèngdiàn.
examples.english: They went to the church to see the holy temple.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恐 is fear.
巩 (gǒng) is a near sound match (-ong).
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: fear is a feeling.
白 (bái) is a close sound clue for pà; 白 also in 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.

example.pinyin: Kǒngpà tā jīntiān búhuì lái le.
example.english: I'm afraid he won't come today.
example.fact: Although both 恐 and 怕 independently mean "to fear," 恐怕 has grammaticalized into a sentence-opening hedge — "I'm afraid that..." — used to soften bad news or an uncertain guess, much like English "I'm afraid" no longer implies the speaker is actually scared.

examples.pinyin: Kǒngpà wǒ méiyǒu shíjiān.
examples.english: I'm afraid I don't have time.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jiàgé kǒngpà tài gāo le.
examples.english: I'm afraid this price is too high.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — cold, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 冻 freeze; here it stands for 氵 water in 準 (a water level, so exact).
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) gives only a loose sound clue for zhǔn.

example.pinyin: Tā de fāyīn hěn zhǔn.
example.english: His pronunciation is very accurate.
example.fact: 准 means accurate (准确) and to allow (不准 "not permitted" is stricter than 不可以). It is also in the everyday 准备 (to prepare) and 准时 (punctual), and as a prefix "quasi", e.g. 准妈妈 (mother-to-be).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhǔnbèi hǎo le ma?
examples.english: Are you ready?

examples.hanzi: 这块表不准，慢了五分钟。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài biǎo bù zhǔn, màn le wǔ fēnzhōng.
examples.english: This watch isn't accurate; it's five minutes slow.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 抢 is grabbing with the hands; also in 打, 拿, 抓.
仓 (cāng) — near sound — 抢 is qiǎng; 仓 also sounds out 枪 qiāng and 创 chuàng.

example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu qiǎng zǒu le tā de bāo.
example.english: The thief snatched her bag away.
example.fact: 抢 is to snatch or rob, and in daily life to rush to get something: 抢票 (grab tickets, a New Year ritual), 抢红包 (grab WeChat red envelopes), 抢购 (panic-buy) and 抢救 (to rescue in an emergency).

examples.pinyin: Bié qiǎng wǒ de wánjù!
examples.english: Don't snatch my toy!

examples.hanzi: 大家都在抢最后一张票。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu zài qiǎng zuìhòu yì zhāng piào.
examples.english: Everyone is scrambling for the last ticket.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and teaching, as in 说, 语, 读; 课 is a lesson.
果 (guǒ) hints at the sound: 课 kè is close to 颗 kē and 棵 kē, which share it.

example.hanzi: 今天下午我们有两节课。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān xiàwǔ wǒmen yǒu liǎng jié kè.
example.english: We have two classes this afternoon.
example.fact: 课 counts class periods with 节: 一节课. You 上课 (go to class), 下课 (class ends), and talk about 课本 (textbook) and 课程 (course). Homework is 作业, not 课.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de kè hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: Today's class is very interesting.

examples.hanzi: 我们明天上午有汉语课。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān shàngwǔ yǒu Hànyǔ kè.
examples.english: We have a Chinese class tomorrow morning.

components.note: 习 (practice) — simplified from 習, a young bird 羽 flapping its wings again and again to learn to fly.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 惯 is what the heart has grown used to.
贯 (guàn) sounds exactly like 惯.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng xíguànle zǎoqǐ.
example.english: I'm already used to getting up early.
example.fact: 习惯 slides between noun ("a habit," 一个好习惯) and verb ("to be used to," 习惯早起) without changing form at all — a flexibility Chinese allows freely that English marks with two separate words.

examples.pinyin: Zǎo shuì zǎo qǐ shì ge hǎo xíguàn.
examples.english: Going to bed and getting up early is a good habit.

examples.hanzi: 我还不习惯这里的天气。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái bù xíguàn zhèlǐ de tiānqì.
examples.english: I'm not yet used to the weather here.

components.note: 王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.

example.hanzi: 梦想和现实总是有差距的。
example.pinyin: Mèngxiǎng hé xiànshí zǒngshì yǒu chājù de.
example.english: There's always a gap between dreams and reality.
example.fact: 现实 reuses the same 现 found in 现在 ("now") — built on 见, "to see" — pairing it with 实 ("solid, true") turns "what is now appearing" into "what is solidly true": reality, as opposed to mere appearance or wish.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào miànduì xiànshí.
examples.english: We have to face reality.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge gùshi hěn xiànshí.
examples.english: This story is very realistic.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 作. 做 is a later variant of 作 zuò (to do), sharing its meaning and sound.
故 (gù) is only a loose sound hint.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zuòchūle xīn de juédìng.
example.english: The government made a new decision.
example.fact: 做出 rarely stands alone — it habitually pairs with a small set of abstract nouns like 决定 (decision), 贡献 (contribution), or 选择 (choice), functioning closer to "to produce X as a result" than the bare dictionary gloss "to put out, to issue" suggests.

examples.hanzi: 他做出了一个重要的决定。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòchūle yí ge zhòngyào de juédìng.
examples.english: He made an important decision.

examples.hanzi: 公司做出了很大的努力。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī zuòchūle hěn dà de nǔlì.
examples.english: The company made a great effort.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — a blade 刂 cutting two jades apart: to divide into groups, hence class or shift.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān bādiǎn shàngbān.
example.english: I go to work at eight every day.
example.fact: 上班 pairs with its neat opposite 下班 ("to get off work") the same way 上车/下车 ("get on/off a vehicle") and 上课/下课 ("start/end class") pair — 上 and 下 ("on" and "off") form one of Mandarin's most productive antonym templates.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān bú shàngbān.
examples.english: I'm not going to work tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ měi tiān zěnme qù shàngbān?
examples.english: How do you get to work every day?

components.note: 身 (body) — marks the body, as in 躲 hide, 躬 bow; 躺 is lying the body down.
尚 (shàng) — loose sound hint (tǎng vs shàng); same part in 堂 táng, 常 cháng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.pinyin: Tā tǎng zài chuáng shang kàn shū.
example.english: He lies in bed reading.
example.fact: 躺 is to lie on your back or side, while 趴 (pā) is to lie face down. 躺平 ("lie flat") became popular internet slang around 2021 for opting out of the rat race.

examples.pinyin: Lèi le jiù tǎng yíhuìr ba.
examples.english: If you're tired, lie down for a while.

examples.pinyin: Tā tǎng zài shāfā shang shuìzháo le.
examples.english: He fell asleep lying on the sofa.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — movement: 起, 超, 趣, 赶; 越 is to cross over, to exceed.
戉 (yuè) sounds exactly like 越.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
走 (walk, run) — movement: 起, 超, 趣, 赶; 越 is to cross over, to exceed.
戉 (yuè) sounds exactly like 越.

example.pinyin: Tiānqì yuèláiyuè lěng le.
example.english: The weather is getting colder and colder.
example.fact: 越来越 collapses the pattern 越...越... ("the more..., the more...") around the verb 来 ("to come") — literally "increasingly coming to increasingly." It must be followed directly by an adjective or verb (越来越冷, 越来越喜欢), never by a bare noun.

examples.pinyin: Tā de Zhōngwén yuè lái yuè hǎo.
examples.english: His Chinese is getting better and better.

examples.pinyin: Lùshang de rén yuè lái yuè duō.
examples.english: There are more and more people on the road.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — a picture of three peaks; as a radical it marks hills, as in 岛, 峰, 岸.

example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù pá shān.
example.english: We're going hiking this weekend.
example.fact: 山 counts with 座 (一座山). 爬山 is hiking, 山水 ("mountains and water") means landscape, especially in painting, and 山 is the radical in many mountain-related characters such as 岛 and 峰.

examples.pinyin: Nà zuò shān hěn gāo, shānshang yǒu xuě.
examples.english: That mountain is very high, with snow on it.

examples.pinyin: Tā jiā zài shān lǐ, kōngqì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: His home is in the mountains, where the air is good.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.
单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.

example.pinyin: Qǐng jiǎnchá yíxià kèrén míngdān.
example.english: Please check the guest list.
example.fact: 名单 transparently combines 名 ("name") with 单, Mandarin's general word for an itemized sheet — the same 单 behind 菜单 ("menu," a list of dishes) and 账单 ("bill," a list of charges).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de míngzi bú zài míngdān shàng.
examples.english: Your name is not on the list.

examples.hanzi: 老师给了我们一份推荐书的名单。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī gěile wǒmen yí fèn tuījiàn shū de míngdān.
examples.english: The teacher gave us a list of recommended books.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
幸 (luck) — often read as an old picture of shackles; 'luck' is escaping punishment. The dictionary story (one alive 土, one dead 干) is a memory aid.
土 (earth) — the top. Memory aid: the one standing on solid ground 土 is the lucky one — 幸运, 幸福.

example.hanzi: 很不幸,他们的车在路上坏了。
example.pinyin: Hěn búxìng, tāmen de chē zài lùshang huài le.
example.english: Unfortunately, their car broke down on the road.
example.fact: 不幸 is simply 幸 ("lucky, fortunate" — also seen in this batch's 幸福, "happiness") negated by 不, giving Mandarin a tidy fortunate/unfortunate pair. Unlike most 不 + adjective negations, 不幸 has settled into common use as a noun in its own right ("a misfortune"), not just a negated adjective.

examples.hanzi: 不幸的是，我们错过了最后一班车。
examples.pinyin: Búxìng de shì, wǒmen cuòguòle zuìhòu yì bān chē.
examples.english: Unfortunately, we missed the last bus.

examples.pinyin: Tā de jiātíng hěn búxìng.
examples.english: His family has been very unfortunate.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 恢 is broad-hearted, then restore.
灰 (huī) sounds exactly like 恢.
复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.

example.pinyin: Tā shēngbìng hòu huīfù de hěn kuài.
example.english: He recovered quickly after being sick.
example.fact: 恢复 covers a wide swath of English's separate verbs "recover, restore, resume" — health (恢复健康), a connection or service (恢复网络), even a past relationship (恢复联系) — letting one Chinese word do the work that English splits across bodies, systems, and situations.

examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò huīfù zhèngcháng le.
examples.english: Work has returned to normal.

examples.pinyin: Wǎngluò hěn kuài jiù huì huīfù.
examples.english: The network will be restored soon.

components.note: 石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".

example.pinyin: Qǐng quèrèn nín de hángbān xìnxī.
example.english: Please confirm your flight information.
example.fact: 确 contributes a sense of solidity (built on 石, "stone") and 认 contributes "to recognize, acknowledge" (built on 讠, "speech") — together 确认 literally means to "firmly acknowledge" something, which is why it feels stronger and more deliberate than a bare 认 alone.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng quèrèn yíxià shíjiān.
examples.english: I'd like to confirm the time.

examples.pinyin: Tā quèrèn zìjǐ méiyǒu tīng cuò.
examples.english: He made sure he hadn't misheard.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is a loose sound clue for jù; the part below shows people gathered together.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 周末我们有一个同学聚会。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen yǒu yígè tóngxué jùhuì.
example.english: We have a classmate gathering this weekend.
example.fact: 聚 alone already means "to assemble" (built from a hand gathering at an ear, plus a cluster of people standing side by side) and 会 separately can mean "to meet" — 聚会 reinforces two near-synonymous "gathering" verbs into one noun, the same synonym-doubling strategy behind 喜欢 and 应该 in the pilot batch.

examples.hanzi: 你来参加我们的聚会吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lái cānjiā wǒmen de jùhuì ba.
examples.english: Come join our party.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā chángcháng zài zhōumò jùhuì.
examples.english: Everyone often gets together at weekends.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 怀 is to cherish something in the heart or bosom.
不 (bù) only stands in for the complicated sound part of traditional 懷 (huái); a loose clue.
子 (child) — children: 孩, 学, 孙; 孕 puts a child inside: pregnant.

example.pinyin: Tā huáiyùn sān gè yuè le.
example.english: She's three months pregnant.
example.fact: 怀 carries a sense of "holding close to the heart" (built on 忄, "heart"), while 孕 pictures a body with a child tucked beneath it (乃 over 子) — 怀孕 literally combines "carrying" with "a child within," a fairly transparent image behind the modern medical term.

examples.hanzi: 她怀孕以后不喝咖啡了。
examples.pinyin: Tā huáiyùn yǐhòu bù hē kāfēi le.
examples.english: She stopped drinking coffee after she became pregnant.

examples.hanzi: 我的姐姐怀孕了，我们都很高兴。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiějie huáiyùn le, wǒmen dōu hěn gāoxìng.
examples.english: My older sister is pregnant and we are all happy.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国 country, 回 return, 图 map; 园 is a fenced garden.
元 (yuán) sounds exactly like 园; also in 远 yuǎn, 院 yuàn, 完 wán.

example.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢在公园里玩。
example.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan zài gōngyuán lǐ wán.
example.english: Children like playing in the park.
example.fact: 园 already means "garden" on its own, as in 花园 ("flower garden") or 果园 ("orchard") — 公园 simply marks that particular garden as "public" (公) rather than private, the same 公 that turns 司 into 公司 ("company," literally a "public office").

examples.hanzi: 我们星期天去公园散步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xīngqītiān qù gōngyuán sànbù.
examples.english: We go for a walk in the park on Sundays.

examples.hanzi: 这个公园里有一个很大的湖。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge gōngyuán lǐ yǒu yí ge hěn dà de hú.
examples.english: There is a big lake in this park.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — cord and silk: 红, 线, 给; 绑 is to bind with cord.
邦 (bāng) is a near sound match for bǎng.
木 (wood) — wooden things: 桌, 板, 桥; 架 is a wooden frame or rack.
加 (jiā) is a near sound match for jià; also in 驾 jià and 嘉 jiā.

example.hanzi: 他被绑架了三天才被救出来。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi bǎngjiàle sān tiān cái bèi jiù chūlái.
example.english: He was kidnapped for three days before being rescued.
example.fact: 绑架 almost always shows up in the passive voice with 被 (被绑架, "to be kidnapped"), since the sentence's focus naturally lands on the victim rather than the kidnapper — a good example of how 被, Mandarin's clearest passive marker, gets reached for almost automatically when something bad happens to someone.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的主角被绑架了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de zhǔjué bèi bǎngjià le.
examples.english: The main character in the movie gets kidnapped.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在调查这起绑架案。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ bǎngjià'àn.
examples.english: The police are investigating this kidnapping case.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.
艹 (grass, plants) — plants and leaves: 花, 草, 叶; 落 is leaves falling.
洛 (luò) sounds exactly like 落; related to 各 gè in 路 lù.

example.hanzi: 这个部落有自己的语言和传统。
example.pinyin: Zhège bùluò yǒu zìjǐ de yǔyán hé chuántǒng.
example.english: This tribe has its own language and traditions.
example.fact: 落 (built on 艹, "plant," originally "to fall," as leaves do) extends by association to a settled cluster of dwellings, a "village" — 部落 pairs that settlement sense with 部 ("a division," also seen in 部门, "department") to name a self-contained community: a tribe.

examples.pinyin: Nà ge bùluò zhù zài shēnshān lǐ.
examples.english: That tribe lives deep in the mountains.

examples.hanzi: 这个部落的人喜欢唱歌跳舞。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge bùluò de rén xǐhuan chànggē tiàowǔ.
examples.english: The people of this tribe like singing and dancing.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — the bottom part, the meat/body radical as in 脑, 脚, 胖. Early forms show meat on a bone, but that does not explain 'willing' today.
止 (stop, foot) — the top. Dictionary story: stop 止 flexing muscle ⺼. Memory aid: you stop resisting and agree — 肯定, a hedged mnemonic.

example.pinyin: Tā bù kěn gàosu wǒ.
example.english: He refuses to tell me.
example.fact: 肯 means to be willing and is most often negated: 不肯 means to refuse. It also builds 肯定 (certain, to affirm) and the pattern 肯 + verb: 他肯帮忙 (he is willing to help).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěndìng huì qù de.
examples.english: I will definitely go.

examples.hanzi: 他不肯帮我，我也没办法。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù kěn bāng wǒ, wǒ yě méi bànfǎ.
examples.english: He won't help me, and there's nothing I can do.
